info.description:
Public, read-only API for Bitrise Insights build and test metrics.

## Authentication
Send a Bitrise API token in the `Authorization` header, either as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` or bare as `Authorization: <token>`. Both forms are
accepted.
Both personal access tokens and workspace API tokens work; the token must have view
access to the workspace in the path and to the project it is queried with.
A missing or malformed header answers 401; a token that is rejected, expired or not
entitled to the workspace or project answers 403.

## Requirements
The Insights API is part of a paid Insights plan. A workspace without one gets 402
on every endpoint.

## Rate limiting
Requests are rate limited per token: 60 requests per minute, across every endpoint
and workspace the token is used with. Every response to a request carrying a
well-formed token carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and
`X-RateLimit-Reset` - the limiter runs once the token is known, so a 401 for a
missing or malformed header has none. Over the limit the API answers 429 with a
`Retry-After` header.

## Conventions
Every call reports on exactly one project, named by the required `project` parameter.
Timestamps are RFC3339 in UTC, both in requests and in responses. Durations are
seconds and rates are percentages in 0-100. Filter parameters that accept several
values are repeated rather than comma-separated: `branch=main&branch=develop`.
The `branch` filter accepts `*` as a wildcard matching any run of characters:
`branch=release/*` matches every release branch.
Responses are long format: one row type per endpoint, and grouping adds a label to
each row instead of changing its shape.

get.description:
The same metrics as builds/totals, grouped by time granularity: one row per bucket,
oldest first, each carrying every metric. Pass 'group_by' to add a dimension
(workflow, pipeline, stage, step): rows keep the same shape and gain that label,
groups are ranked by build count and capped by 'limit'.
The window may span at most 7 days hourly, 90 days daily, 1 year weekly and
2 years monthly.

Grouped, the response has one row per bucket per group - for example per day per
workflow - and each row names its group in the matching field ('workflow' here).
get.summary: Get a build metrics time series for a project.

parameters.description: Slug of the workspace the project belongs to
parameters.name: workspace_slug

parameters.description:
Keeps only builds that ran on one of these git branches. Repeat the parameter for several
values: branch=main&branch=develop. '*' matches any run of characters, so branch=release/*
keeps every release branch. Omit to include every branch.
parameters.name: branch

parameters.description: End of the reported time window, exclusive, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Must be after 'start'.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description:
Size of one time bucket. It also caps how long a window may be: 7 days hourly, 90 days
daily, 1 year weekly, 2 years monthly.
parameters.name: granularity

parameters.description:
Splits the series by one more dimension. Without it the response has one row per time
bucket for the whole project. With group_by=workflow it has one row per time bucket per
workflow, each row carrying the workflow's name in its 'workflow' field - and likewise for
pipeline, stage and step. One dimension per call.
parameters.name: group_by

parameters.description:
Caps how many groups are returned, keeping those with the most builds. Ignored when
'group_by' is omitted. See 'truncated' in the response to tell whether groups were dropped.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Keeps only builds of one of these pipelines. Repeatable, like 'branch'.
parameters.name: pipeline

parameters.description: ID of the project to report on. Exactly one is required.
parameters.name: project

parameters.description: Start of the reported time window, inclusive, as an RFC3339 timestamp.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: Keeps only builds of one of these workflows. Repeatable, like 'branch'.
parameters.name: workflow

get.description:
Test cases that were rerun after a flaky result in the requested time window, one
page at a time, ranked by 'order_by' (flaky_rerun_count or flaky_rate).
The window may span at most 2 years.
get.summary: List the flaky test cases of a project.

parameters.description: Slug of the workspace the project belongs to
parameters.name: workspace_slug

parameters.description:
Keeps only test runs from builds that ran on one of these git branches. Repeat the parameter
for several values: branch=main&branch=develop. '*' matches any run of characters, so
branch=release/* keeps every release branch. Omit to include every branch.
parameters.name: branch

parameters.description:
End of the reported time window, exclusive, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Must be after 'start',
and may span at most 2 years.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: Keeps only test cases of one of these modules. Repeatable, like 'branch'.
parameters.name: module

parameters.description: Direction of the ranking.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description:
Ranks the list. The default puts the flakiest first by absolute rerun count rather than by
rate, so a test case that fails intermittently across thousands of runs outranks one that was
rerun twice out of three.
parameters.name: order_by

parameters.description: Page of the result set to return, 1-based.

parameters.description: Test cases per page. See 'pagination' in the response for the total and the next page.
